title: Session Cliff analysis — latency & cost quickscan
content:
Purpose
Quick internal sketch to capture a small benchmark sweep we ran to understand a recurring pattern we call the "session cliff": a sudden jump in p99 latency and $/query when a small fraction of sessions cross a length threshold (e.g. prefix + user turn > 1024 tokens). This doc is a working quickscan — rough numbers, ASCII charts, and immediate recommendations for console and Optimize teams.

What we tested (configs)
- Models: small-open-v1 (13B), conv-lite-7B, demo-compat-3B-quant
- Execution profiles: baseline (no prefetch), tiling (slotized tiling), prefix-prefetch (intent-aware prefetch of KV for recent prefixes)
- Quantization: fp16 vs int8 (for demo-compat only)
- Workload: synthetic session mix derived from production 2025-12 sample: 92% short (<128 tokens), 6% mid (128-1024), 2% long (>1024). We focused on the long tail (the 2%).

Key raw table (p50/p90/p99 in ms, $/query approximated across token amortization):

+----------------------+---------+---------+---------+---------+
| Config               | p50 ms  | p90 ms  | p99 ms  | $/query |
+----------------------+---------+---------+---------+---------+
| baseline (13B fp16)  | 38      | 86      | 420     | 0.0092  |
| tiling (13B fp16)    | 42      | 78      | 210     | 0.0071  |
| prefetch (13B fp16)  | 45      | 70      | 160     | 0.0068  |
| baseline (7B fp16)   | 22      | 48      | 240     | 0.0054  |
| tiling (7B fp16)     | 26      | 44      | 130     | 0.0043  |
| prefetch (7B fp16)   | 28      | 40      | 95      | 0.0041  |
| demo-compat (3B int8)| 18      | 36      | 88      | 0.0028  |
+----------------------+---------+---------+---------+---------+

Observations
- The p99 cliff is most visible on baseline runs: long sessions cause decoder stalls and cache churn that blow up p99 by 2–6x versus p90.
- Tiling reduces p99 substantially (roughly 40–50% of baseline p99) but increases p50 slightly — consistent with slotization overhead on short sessions.
- Prefix-prefetch outperforms tiling on p99 and $/query for long sessions by keeping KV_cache warm; overhead on short sessions is minimal.
- Int8 (3B) shows best $/query but p99 still sensitive to session shape; combining int8 + prefetch yielded the best cost-latency tradeoff in our sweep.

ASCII sparkline (p99 fragility across session percentiles)
- short(0–90%): ▂▂▂▂▂  (stable)
- mid(90–98%): ▂▇▇▃  (rising)
- long(98–100%): ▇▇▇▇▇  (cliff)

Cribbed notes / hypotheses
- Root cause: KV cache eviction thrash when a small number of requests include long context that grows KV and forces recompute on shared slots.
- Tiling helps by bounding working set per slot; prefetch mitigates miss penalties by async warming.
- There is a scheduling component: multiplex backpressure and admission control can amplify observed p99 when long sessions pile onto scarce fast-path GPUs.

Immediate action items (short-term)
- (Eng-Console) Add per-route "session-cliff alert" in Console: flag routes with >0.5% sessions crossing 1k tokens and p99 uplift >x2. Owner: Jamal. ETA: 2 wks.
- (Runtime) Prototype a prefix-prefetch flag in runtime that can be toggled per-model/per-route; instrument KV hits. Owner: Lin. ETA: 3 wks.
- (Optimize) Add a suggested knob in Optimize UI: "aggressiveness: prefetch|tiling|baseline" with expected p99 and $ delta. Owner: Marina. ETA: 4 wks.

Open questions / next experiments
- Measure interaction with dynamic batching: does batching amplify or dampen the cliff? need sweep with varying batch windows.
- Quantize + tiling interplay for medium models (13B int8) — prototype build pending.
- Region routing: would offloading long-session handling to lower-cost, higher-memory machines reduce observed p99 without hurting throughput?

Notes to self / TODOs
- Attach raw CSVs and trace slices (CONFLUENCE-REQ-3245) — Jamal to upload.
- Follow-up UX mock for Optimize knob (Marina) and link to PR when ready.
- Run longer 24h soak with production-weighted session mix to validate edge behavior (schedule for 2026-02-22).

Appendix: brief experiment methodology
- Each measurement is the median of 5 runs, 30k synthetic sessions per run, seeded from production session-length histogram.
- All runs executed on same hardware family (A100-equivalent hosts), runtime commit: PR 981.
- Cost estimates are rough amortizations using token counts and GPU-time unit pricing, intended for comparison only (not billing).

If you want a condensed slide for the next sync, I can convert key tables into two slides: (1) p99 cliff visualization + recommendation, (2) immediate knobs and owners. Feedback welcome — this is rough and I expect numbers to shift after the 24h soak.
